slides.title: Rules & Regulations
slides.content:
1. Obligation (Necessary)

To say something is a rule, we use:

  • Must: "You must wear an ID badge." (Strong rule)
  • Have to: "I have to finish this report." (External obligation)

2. Prohibition vs. No Necessity (CRITICAL)

Must NOT: It is forbidden.
"You must not smoke here."
Don't have to: It is not necessary (optional).
"You don't have to wear a tie."
slides.speech_text: In a company, rules are important. Use MUST or HAVE TO for obligations. But be careful: MUST NOT means it is forbidden. DON'T HAVE TO means it is optional. There is a big difference!

slides.title: Safety Briefing
slides.content: Listen to the Safety Officer talking to new visitors.
slides.audio_script:
Officer: Welcome to the factory floor. Before we enter, let's review the rules.
        Visitor: Do I have to wear a helmet?
        Officer: Yes, absolutely. Everyone must wear a helmet and safety glasses at all times.
        Visitor: And what about my camera? Can I take photos?
        Officer: No, you must not take photos inside. It is strictly forbidden.
        Visitor: Do we need to sign out when we leave?
        Officer: No, you don't have to sign out, just return the badge.

quiz.question: What items MUST the visitor wear?

slides.title: Roleplay: New Employee Orientation
slides.system_prompt:
You are an HR Manager explaining office rules.
        The user is a new employee asking questions.
        
        Steps:
        1. Welcome the employee.
        2. Answer their questions about dress code (Casual Friday - don't have to wear a tie).
        3. Answer their questions about working hours (Must start at 9 AM).
        4. Explain a prohibition (Must not eat at the desk).
        
        Goal: Use Modals (Must, Have to, Don't have to) correctly in your answers.
slides.initial_message: Welcome to the team! Do you have any questions about our office rules?
slides.user_goal: Ask about the dress code (clothes) and lunch rules.
